prompt.context:
Howell Blanchard (HB) is a multinational enterprise IT company with $40 billion in annual revenue. Founded in 1941, HB is a Silicon Valley cornerstone that focuses on enterprise hardware solutions such as servers, networking, and storage. As part of the firm's operating model, annual IT operational expenditure (opex) is budgeted at 1.5% of revenue. Currently, the company is hitting that target with an annual IT run rate of $600 million.

Recently, HB announced that it would be merging with rival hardware maker Crisco in a mega-deal to create one of the largest public companies in the U.S. Crisco's annual revenue is $50 billion, but it has a larger IT spend, at $1 billion, or 2% of revenue. The CEO of HB, who will lead the combined entity, has internal estimates of $95 billion in revenue for the combined entity in its first fiscal year and has set the first year IT budget at $1.425 billion. Given this target, the combined entity needs to reduce costs by $175 million through the integration process.

Your firm is the lead integration partner for HB, and HB's CIO has asked the firm's Technology M&A partner on the project to develop a strategic plan for HB on consolidation, cost reduction, and integration planning so it can achieve its budget target. As a consultant on the project, you are responsible for putting the initial deck together for review with the partner.
prompt.question: How would you approach consolidating and rationalizing HB's and Crisco's software applications and creating synergistic business processes during integration?

clarifying_info.q: What is the combined IT spend before any reductions?
clarifying_info.a: HB spends $600M and Crisco spends $1B, totaling $1.6B combined. The target is $1.425B, requiring a $175M reduction.

clarifying_info.q: Who will lead the combined entity and whose systems will be used?
clarifying_info.a: The HB CEO will lead the combined entity. All HB systems should be migrated onto Crisco's systems so that all business activities originate from Crisco's systems on Day 1.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a deadline for the integration?
clarifying_info.a: The HB CEO has given a date 10 months out by which the two companies will officially begin operations as 'HBC' and be traded on Wall Street as such.

clarifying_info.q: What ERP systems are both companies currently using?
clarifying_info.a: Both HB and Crisco are running older versions of SAP's ERP system and would like to upgrade to the new SAP S4/HANA system as part of the integration.

framework: People: Assess the business impact of combining, removing, or migrating employees onto new systems; manage change and training
Process: Evaluate shared business processes (finance, operations, sales and marketing); identify opportunities to streamline and realize synergies through integration
Technology: Catalogue, rationalize, and consolidate applications, labor, and infrastructure in alignment with the combined entity's (HBC) business goals

questions.prompt: How would you approach consolidating and rationalizing HB's and Crisco's software applications and creating synergistic business processes during integration?
questions.guidance: A strong answer uses a structured framework such as People / Process / Technology (P/P/T). Under People, candidate discusses business impact of combining or removing systems and ramping employees onto new platforms. Under Process, candidate addresses how shared functions (finance, ops, sales & marketing) must be evaluated and leveraged to realize synergies, and how integration is an opportunity to streamline existing processes. Under Technology, candidate describes cataloguing, rationalizing, and consolidating applications, labor, and infrastructure based on alignment with HBC's business goals.

questions.prompt: What would be some key components to IT cost reduction efforts in order to help HB-Crisco reduce its IT spend and meet its $1.425B target?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify multiple IT cost reduction strategies, potentially including: application rationalization; data center / server / storage / networking consolidation and optimization; cloud strategies (e.g., IaaS via AWS or SaaS via switching to Salesforce); end-user device rationalization (PCs, telephony, mobile); outsourcing (application maintenance, help desk, development support); vendor contract renegotiation. Excellent candidates articulate the potential impact of each lever on IT cost structure (applications, labor, infrastructure).

math.setup: Combined IT spend = HB $600M + Crisco $1,000M = $1,600M. Target = $1,425M. Required reduction = $1,600M - $1,425M = $175M.

questions.prompt: Given the Day 1 requirements of the merger (all operations to originate from Crisco's systems in 10 months), how would you approach the project efforts to merge and upgrade the two companies' ERP systems?
questions.guidance: A strong answer outlines the phases of the SDLC: identification, planning, analysis, design, implementation, and maintenance. Candidate should note that a 'big bang' implementation methodology is required to meet the Day 1 requirements (as opposed to a phased rollout or pilot approach). Excellent candidates discuss the merits and risks of the big bang approach and contrast it with phased and pilot alternatives, while explaining why the Day 1 constraint forces the big bang decision. Knowledge of the SAP S4/HANA upgrade adds depth.

brainstorming.prompt: What are three tech trends that you are following and why are they important?

categories.name: Cloud & Infrastructure
ideas: Migration of enterprise workloads to public cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP)
Hybrid cloud and multi-cloud strategies for enterprise resilience
Serverless and containerization (Kubernetes) reducing infrastructure overhead

categories.name: Artificial Intelligence & Automation
ideas: Generative AI and large language models transforming enterprise workflows
AI-driven IT operations (AIOps) for predictive incident management
Robotic process automation (RPA) eliminating repetitive back-office tasks

categories.name: Cybersecurity
ideas: Zero-trust architecture replacing perimeter-based security models
Rise of ransomware and supply chain attacks driving security investment
SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) converging networking and security

categories.name: Data & Analytics
ideas: Real-time data streaming and edge analytics for operational intelligence
Data mesh architectures decentralizing data ownership across business units
Privacy-enhancing computation (e.g., federated learning) for compliant analytics

recommendation: Adopt a People / Process / Technology framework to drive the integration, ensuring each workstream has a clear owner and milestone
Prioritize the $175M cost reduction through application rationalization, data center consolidation, cloud migration, and vendor renegotiation
Execute the SAP S4/HANA ERP migration using a 'big bang' approach to meet the 10-month Day 1 deadline, with rigorous SDLC governance from identification through implementation
risks: Big bang ERP go-live carries high execution risk; a failure on Day 1 could disrupt $95B in combined revenue operations
Employee resistance and change management challenges could delay system adoption and erode expected synergies
Aggressive 10-month timeline may compress testing phases, increasing the probability of post-go-live defects
next_steps: Stand up an integration management office (IMO) with dedicated People, Process, and Technology workstreams
Commission an application and infrastructure inventory across both HB and Crisco within the first 30 days
Engage SAP and a systems integrator immediately to begin SDLC planning for the S4/HANA upgrade and migration
